newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung, China discuss handover celebrations.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung, China discuss handover celebrations.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa conferred with Chinese officials in the south China city of Shenzhen on Monday over planned celebrations to mark the territory's return to Beijing's control.
Tung crossed the border to meet China's ruling State Council secretary-general Luo Gan, a statement by Tung's office.
The post-colonial leader will take over from Governor Chris Patten when the British pull out at midnight on June 30, sparking celebrations on both sides of the border.
The statement did not elaborate on the agenda for Tung's one-day visit to the booming city of Shenzhen.

Britain and China have announced they will stage a glitzy ceremony at midnight on June 30 at the new extension of Hong Kong convention centre, attended by 4,000 dignitaries, including U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Britain's heir to the throne Prince Charles will lead the British delegation. However, it is not clear who will be most senior Chinese official attending the ceremony marking the end of 156 years of British colonial rule.
